title: C1046 — Inline connector reference
introduction:
I use this inline-connector reference like a street directory: the drawing locates a cavity, and the matching table row explains its electrical address. Start with the connector identity and harness heading, find the printed cavity label, then read across the circuit, color, gauge, function, qualifier and terminal fields. Similar-looking wires are a poor substitute for matching the whole row.

The illustrated outer columns count upward from the bottom; the middle column has more widely spaced positions. Gray-filled positions correspond to blank circuit entries in the respective face table. Use the printed labels rather than counting circles. The housing outline helps distinguish the drawing, but its projections do not establish how to release the connector.

This is a circuit-identification reference. It does not establish the physical viewing direction, access, probing method, test conditions or repair procedure. Keep the Size, Used and gauge entries as recorded without assuming undocumented conventions. Read fuse-or-circuit-breaker descriptions literally; neither alternative can be selected from this reference alone. The summary Pin Count disagrees with the numbered positions in both drawings. That discrepancy remains unresolved and does not establish extra physical cavities. The tables also contain unqualified alternative functions, colors, gauges and terminals; they do not identify which configuration applies.

edits.why: The harness and gender identify which face table belongs with this drawing. They do not establish whether a physical connector should be viewed from its terminal side or wire side.

Read each row across before interpreting its function. Generator regulator control and generator load input have distinct labels, just as a command and a report have different jobs. Keep signal returns, sensor supplies, network lines and relay functions distinct; a relay label alone does not establish a separate plug-in component. Blank circuit fields describe an unassigned entry here, not a diagnosed fault. Preserve repeated entries without choosing a circuit, gauge or terminal where applicability is unresolved.

Use this face’s own printed labels: its outer columns reverse their left/right placement relative to the male drawing, while the middle column retains its more widely spaced positions. This is a description of the supplied drawings, not a physical viewing-side or release instruction.

Read this table independently rather than copying the male-side colors, gauges or terminals. The unqualified compressor-valve and oxygen-sensor alternatives remain distinct, as do the repeated oxygen-sensor color entries. A matching cavity label does not resolve those alternatives or establish an electrical test point.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata gives Pin Count as 41, while the attached face drawing shows numbered positions through 34. The supplied evidence does not reconcile these descriptions; confirm the intended count and drawing association.

Cavity 28 lists both VE462 for the variable A/C compressor valve and VE733 for the post-catalyst oxygen sensor. Cavity 29 lists CBK03, CE234 and RE249 with different functions. Their Qualifier fields are blank, so the applicable assignments cannot be selected.

The repeated cavity 27 entries retain RE249 but differ in gauge and terminal part number, with no applicability qualifier. Keep these alternatives visible pending clarification rather than presenting a single terminal specification.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 105 primary units, six complete pages/two figures and four edits. Original first CLI author covered 54 units/two male headings. Complete draft includes both connector faces and discloses count and assignment discrepancies. Original partial author retained separately; physical count, color, gauge and assignment alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
